checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: All four lines spoken exactly, in order, no labels
must.why: Audio not transcribed; only that sound exists.

must.item: Two distinct voices, A lower, B higher
must.why: Man and woman are visible, which suggests lower and higher voices, but audio is unheard.

must.item: Each voice reads its assigned lines
must.why: Cannot hear who speaks which line; frames show no clear lip sync.

must.item: Friendly, natural, about 8 s, no overlaps or cut-offs
must.why: Duration is 8 s and the people look friendly, but the speech is unheard.

must.item: One standalone audio file, no music/SFX
must.why: The deliverable is an MP4 video link, not an audio file. The user explicitly said no video, and the agent only said to convert it themselves.

exact_text.read_as: No on-screen text; this is spoken audio and cannot be checked from frames.

exact_text.text: Almost. Have you got the tickets?

faults.what: The deliverable is a video (MP4) although the user said 'no video, just audio'. The user has to extract the audio themselves.
The frames show a scene change from the doorway at 0.8 s to a static pose at 5.6 s. The two stand facing the camera, which looks staged.
The man in the doorway at 0.8 s looks different from the later frames: the door has moved and the lighting has changed. This is some scene inconsistency.

summary: The agent made an 8 s video of a man and a woman talking in a doorway, with sound, but the user asked for audio only. The spoken lines, voices and order cannot be verified from the frames, and no standalone audio file was delivered.
